card.flavorText: The 511th Parachute Infantry Regiment was a unit of the 11th Airborne Division during WWII. The division was activated in 1943 and trained for airborne assaults, jungle warfare, and amphibious operations. Its first major engagement came during the Philippines Campaign, where it was involved in intense fighting on Leyte in late 1944. It is particularly celebrated for its role in the liberation of Luzon in early 1945. In a famous raid, the 11th Airborne liberated over 2,000 Allied POWs from the Los Baños Internment Camp, a bold operation involving airborne and amphibious elements which caught the Japanese forces by surprise. The division continued to see action on Luzon until the Japanese surrender, earning a distinguished reputation for resilience and bravery in some of the toughest conditions of the Pacific campaign. After the war, the 11th Airborne Division served in the occupation of Japan, helping to maintain security and assisting in postwar reconstruction efforts until they were recalled to the United States in 1949.
